note: Direct end-to-end simulation of genuine qMPS and qTTN parameterized circuits (not projection). Observable = <Z_c Z_c'> at the canonical centre; gradient wrt a canonical-centre parameter via exact parameter-shift; 1500 random parameter draws per point; gate set {RY,RZ,CNOT}; run on uicgpu. The qTTN N=16 point was terminated for runtime (single 16384-dim tree point exceeded ~30 min); N=4,8 qTTN points suffice to establish the shallower decay.

qmps.interpretation: Exponential decay in N (barren plateau), c = 1/0.683 = 1.46 > 1.

qttn.interpretation: Much shallower decay (power-law-consistent, Var ~ N^-1.4). qMPS decays 1.59x steeper per qubit than qTTN over the same N range.

conclusion: Direct simulation reproduces the paper's central dichotomy: qMPS gradient variance decays exponentially in N (barren plateau) while qTTN decays only mildly/polynomially (trainable). C1 (E[grad]=0) confirmed: all measured mean gradients are O(1e-3), scattered in sign.
